description: Shared, language-neutral test cases for computeContainerLayout's behavior. Every case here was extracted from, or verified directly against, @fluida/core's TypeScript implementation and its existing unit tests — not invented independently. This is a shared set of inputs and expected outputs, not a formal specification: it exists so any current or future implementation (in any language) can be checked against the same real cases the TypeScript implementation already passes.

tolerance.note: columns and rows must match exactly. cellWidth and cellHeight must be within max(absoluteMinimum, abs(expected) * relative) of the expected value — a relative tolerance with an absolute floor, so exact-zero expectations (e.g. the not-yet-fitting fallback) still allow a tiny epsilon instead of demanding bit-exact equality.

cases.description: No strategy, gap, or aspectRatio given — defaults to fit, gap 16, aspectRatio 1. Also demonstrates an irregular item count (8 items do not divide evenly into any column count without leftover cells) and a decimal (non-integer) result.
Explicit fit strategy: square cells, sized to the smaller dimension of the unconstrained fill answer.
Fill strategy: uses the exact available space in both axes, even though the resulting cell is not square.

Balanced strategy: each axis is the geometric mean of the fill answer's own value and the safe square size (min of the two) — the smaller fill dimension is unchanged, the larger one is pulled toward it without exceeding it.

Balanced on a much wider-than-tall container: cellHeight must equal containerHeight exactly (the constraining axis), never exceed it — this is the case the geometric-mean-of-two-values formula used to overflow on.
preserve-ratio with an integer aspect ratio (2): the cell keeps exactly that width-to-height ratio.
preserve-ratio with a fractional (non-integer) aspect ratio, 16/9 — the same widescreen ratio used throughout the project's own demo and documentation.
gap explicitly set to 0, and minItemWidth omitted entirely — an integer result (100x100), and the baseline that the minItemWidth-reduces-columns case below is compared against.
Container with no measured size yet (width and height both 0) — the honest not-yet-fitting fallback, not an error.

Same container and item count as gap-zero-integer-result, but with minItemWidth: 150 — 4 columns of 100px each would be excluded (100 < 150), leaving 2 columns of 200px as the widest still-eligible option.

minItemWidth checked against a cell width that already has gap subtracted: with a 16px gap, 5 columns would need (1200 - 4*16) / 5 = 227.2px per cell, below the 280px minimum, so 5 columns is excluded and 4 columns (288px) wins instead.
minItemWidth set higher than any column count could ever satisfy in this container — falls back to the same not-yet-fitting shape as zero-size-container, not a distinct error.
minItemWidth filters eligible columns first; fit then squares off whatever candidate survived that filter — same 2-column, 200x50 candidate as min-item-width-reduces-columns, squared down to 50x50.
minItemWidth filters eligible columns first; preserve-ratio then applies its configured aspect ratio on top of the same surviving candidate.
A prime, irregular item count (7) that cannot divide evenly into any small grid.
A single item — the simplest possible case, one column and one row, filling the whole measured space.
A wider, shallower container with more items and a smaller gap than the other cases — an integer result at a different scale than gap-zero-integer-result.

containerHeight omitted (null): fit chooses columns from width and minItemWidth alone, then squares the cell — same columns and cellWidth as the height-aware min-item-width-accounts-for-gap case above, confirming the two paths agree whenever both could apply.

containerHeight omitted (null): preserve-ratio chooses the same columns as auto-height-fit (same width, gap, minItemWidth), then derives cellHeight from cellWidth and aspectRatio directly — never limited by a height that doesn't exist.
containerHeight omitted (null): a column count whose cellWidth lands exactly on minItemWidth (1000 / 5 columns, gap 0 = exactly 200) is accepted, not excluded — the boundary is inclusive.
